principles: An offer refused on the ground of strength

world_behind.title: Ammoron offers a city for prisoners
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has him propose Antiparah in exchange. Helaman refuses in verse 2, saying their forces are sufficient to take it.

world_behind.title: The city falls without a fight
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says the people of Antiparah left and fled to other cities. The refusal in verse 2 turns out to have been correct.

world_behind.title: Sixty more sons arrive
world_behind.text: Verse 6 adds them to the two thousand, which is why the number is two thousand and sixty from here on.

world_behind.title: A prisoner revolt costs a thousand Nephites
world_behind.text: Verses 14 through 19 have the prisoners rise during a battle and the escort kill many of them, while the main Lamanite army attacks.

world_behind.title: The two thousand and sixty hold when the rest give way
world_behind.text: Verse 20 says the remainder of the army was about to break and the young men were firm and undaunted.

world_behind.title: Helaman remembers what they told him
world_behind.text: Verse 21 has him recall the words about their mothers, in the middle of a battle report.

world_behind.title: The count is exact and qualified
world_behind.text: Verse 25 gives two hundred fainted from loss of blood, none dead, and not one without many wounds.

words.text: A city held by the Lamanites on the southern border. The name occurs seven times in this record, all in Alma 56 and 57. Taking it is the campaign this chapter reports.
Not made afraid. The word occurs once in scripture. It describes the two thousand and sixty at the moment the rest of the army was about to give way.
Precision in carrying something out. The word occurs once in scripture. Helaman uses it of how the young men obeyed every word of command, and he pairs it in the same verse with their faith.
Treated at Alma 43:19, of clothing. Here Helaman uses the word of wounds, in the order he gives immediately after the Lamanites flee. Care for the wounded is the first thing he does.

Lost consciousness. The record uses it six times and the King James Bible twelve. Helaman applies it to two hundred of his young men, and the number is what makes the survival remarkable rather than trivial.

To attribute, to assign a cause. The word occurs once in this record and three times in the King James Bible, all of ascribing greatness to God. Helaman uses it of the preservation and marks the ascription as just.

phrases.term: By delivering up the prisoners for that city we should suppose ourselves unwise
phrases.text: Helaman's refusal, argued on value. He judges his own force sufficient to take Antiparah, so trading prisoners for it would be paying twice.

phrases.term: The people of Antiparah did leave the city, and fled
phrases.text: The city Ammoron offered is abandoned. Helaman's judgment in verse 2 is confirmed two verses later, and he reports it without comment.

phrases.term: Sixty of the sons of the Ammonites who had come to join their brethren
phrases.text: The reinforcement that changes the count. From here the record says two thousand and sixty, and the arithmetic in verse 25 depends on it.

phrases.term: My little band of two thousand and sixty fought most desperately
phrases.text: Helaman's own phrase for them. Little band sits against the size of the armies around it, and desperately is the word he chooses for how they fought.

phrases.term: Those two thousand and sixty were firm and undaunted
phrases.text: The contrast with the rest of the army, stated plainly. The remainder was giving way; these did not.

phrases.term: They did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness
phrases.text: Helaman names obedience before faith in the same verse. The precision of their soldiering is reported as part of the reason things went as they did.

phrases.term: I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them
phrases.text: A commander recalling a conversation while writing up a battle. Alma 56 recorded the words; here they come back to him at the point of survival.

phrases.term: To whom we owe this great victory
phrases.text: Helaman assigns the credit to the young men and to the prisoner escort. He names both groups and does not include himself.

phrases.term: There was not one soul of them who did perish; yea, and neither was there one soul among them who had not received many wounds
phrases.text: The claim and its qualification in one verse. None dead, all wounded, two hundred unconscious from blood loss.

phrases.term: That they should be spared while there was a thousand of our brethren who were slain
phrases.text: Helaman states the comparison that makes the preservation astonishing. He does not explain why the thousand died, and he does not soften the number.

phrases.term: Their minds are firm, and they do put their trust in God continually
phrases.text: Helaman's summary of the two thousand and sixty. He offers it as a description of what he has seen rather than as a general rule about young men.

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: Antiparah
verses.text: Ammoron offers the city for the prisoners. Helaman refuses, judging his force sufficient, and offers only a straight exchange. Ammoron refuses that. The Nephites prepare to attack, and the people of Antiparah abandon the city, which falls without a battle.

verses.label: v. 6–12
verses.title: Cumeni
verses.text: Six thousand men and provisions arrive, with sixty more sons of the Ammonites. They surround Cumeni by night and intercept its supply convoys until the Lamanites surrender the city. The prisoners are so numerous that they strain the guard and the food.

verses.label: v. 13–19
verses.title: The revolt
verses.text: The prisoners are sent to Zarahemla under escort. They rise against the escort on the way, and many are killed. The remaining Lamanite army attacks Cumeni, and the fighting is desperate. Helaman's little band fights most desperately of all.

verses.label: v. 20–23
verses.title: The stand
verses.text: The rest of the army is about to give way, and the two thousand and sixty are firm and undaunted, obeying every word of command with exactness. Helaman remembers what they told him about their mothers. He credits them and the escort with the victory, and the city is held at great cost.

verses.label: v. 24–27
verses.title: The count
verses.text: He orders the wounded taken from among the dead and their wounds dressed. Two hundred had fainted from loss of blood, and not one of them died, though none escaped many wounds. Their preservation astonishes the army, and Helaman ascribes it to God because of their faith in what they were taught.

verses.label: v. 28–36
verses.title: The aftermath
verses.text: Gid reports what happened with the prisoners: the revolt, the killing, and the flight of the rest to join the Lamanite army. The Nephites hold Cumeni and Manti remains in Lamanite hands. Helaman's forces are too few to take it.

chapter.title: A refusal is vindicated by events
chapter.text: Helaman declines to buy a city he believes he can take, and two verses later its people abandon it. Mormon lets the sequence make the point.

chapter.title: The number changes and the record tracks it
chapter.text: Two thousand becomes two thousand and sixty in verse 6, and every later count uses the new figure. The arithmetic in verse 25 depends on the bookkeeping.

chapter.title: Obedience is named before faith
chapter.text: Verse 21 gives exactness in carrying out commands first, then says it was done to them according to their faith. Helaman reports both as operative.

chapter.title: The commander credits everyone else
chapter.text: Verse 22 names the young men and the prisoner escort as those to whom the victory is owed. Helaman is writing to his own superior and takes none of it.

chapter.title: The claim is stated with its limits
chapter.text: None died; all were wounded; two hundred lost consciousness. The record gives the striking fact and immediately makes it precise.

chapter.title: The thousand dead are counted too
chapter.text: Verse 26 sets the preservation against a thousand Nephite deaths in the same battle. Helaman does not explain the difference and does not hide it.

chapter.title: The ascription is called just
chapter.text: Not asserted as obvious. Helaman says they do justly ascribe it to God, which marks the conclusion as one he has weighed.

chapter.title: The letter keeps returning to the mothers
chapter.text: Alma 56 gave the teaching; Alma 57 has Helaman remembering it mid-battle and citing it as the content of the faith. The two chapters build one argument.

applications.title: Do not pay for what you can do
applications.text: Helaman refused a trade for a city he thought he could take. Before accepting a costly deal, ask honestly whether you already have what it takes.

applications.title: Dress the wounds first
applications.text: Helaman's first order after the enemy fled was to find the wounded among the dead. When a crisis passes, attend to the people who are still hurt before anything else.

applications.title: Do it with exactness
applications.text: The young men performed every word of command precisely. Where you have been given specific instructions, consider whether you have been approximating them.

applications.title: Count and then say where the credit goes
applications.text: Helaman named two groups and left himself out. After something goes well, be specific about who did it.

questions.text: What am I about to buy that I could simply do?
Who has recently joined what I am doing, and did I welcome them?
When everyone around me is giving way, what holds me?
Which instruction have I been carrying out approximately?
Who around me is wounded and lying among people who look fine?
What good outcome have I received while others did not?
Is my mind firm, and what would make it firmer?
